units.title: Introduction to Computers
units.overview: This chapter introduces what a computer is, its definition, characteristics, capabilities and limitations, and major application areas.
units.summary: A computer is an electronic device that accepts input, processes data according to instructions (programs), and produces output. It can store information, process large amounts of data quickly, and work continuously. Computers are used in education, business, healthcare, communication, entertainment, and science. They have both capabilities (speed, accuracy, storage, automation) and limitations (no own intelligence, dependency on humans, environment needs).

detailed.heading: Chapter 1 — Introduction to Computers
detailed.note: Notes for Chapter 1 of the Class 6 book: what a computer is, the five characteristics that define it, what it can and cannot do, and the fields it is used in.

blocks.text: Computers were invented to help people solve problems and make tasks easier to do. Since the first ones were built they have changed out of all recognition — becoming faster, more powerful and easier to use.

They are used in many different ways today: for work, for fun, for learning, and for talking to other people. They come in different shapes and sizes — desktops, laptops, tablets and smartphones — and they can do many different things: play games, type documents, browse the internet, send emails and make art.
The word "computer" comes from the Latin word computare, which means to calculate. That is where the machine began — but it is not where it ended.
A fast electronic data processing device. It processes the input data according to instructions given by the programmer or user, and produces the desired information as output at high speed.
The working process of a computer
Everything a computer does follows the same three steps:

items: Input — data and instructions go in.
Process — the data is manipulated and calculated.
Output — the result comes out.

blocks.title: Data and information are not the same
blocks.text: Data is raw — a list of marks, say. Information is what you get once the data has been processed and means something, such as a class average. The computer turns one into the other.
Five features set a computer apart from the tools that came before it.

items: Speed. Data processing is very fast. A computer finishes in seconds what might take a person many days, handling millions or billions of instructions in a second.

Accuracy. A computer is more accurate than a person — its accuracy is about 100%. But that comes with a condition: it produces accurate output only if the inputs given to it are accurate. Wrong input gives wrong output, which is known as GIGO — Garbage In, Garbage Out.
Automation. A computer is an automatic machine. Once instructions are fed to it, it works by itself without human intervention, as long as there is a well-defined procedure to follow.
Diligence. It can perform repetitive tasks without being bored and never gets tired, working efficiently for hours or days on end.
Versatility. It can be used in different areas for different tasks using different programs — from simple arithmetic to highly complex logical manipulation.

blocks.title: Versatility in practice
blocks.text: At one moment a computer can play music; at the same time it can be downloading from the internet while you work on a spreadsheet, a document and a presentation. That is what versatility looks like.
Capabilities

items: It can perform a task automatically.
It can process with 100% accuracy.
It can perform different tasks in different fields.
It can perform repetitive tasks without getting tired.

blocks.text: Limitations

items: It is a dull machine.
It cannot think and make the right decisions as a human being can.
It cannot operate without electricity or a power supply.
It cannot produce accurate output if the inputs are wrong.

blocks.title: The important one
blocks.text: The second limitation is the one to remember: a computer follows instructions, it does not understand them. It cannot judge, and it cannot decide what should be done — only carry out what it has been told.

The computer is the most powerful device people have made, and it plays a part in almost every field of life — education, business, offices, communication, banks, hospitals, industry, robotics and more.
1. Computer in education
Used for learning: online classes, online examinations, online tutoring, reading e-books, practical exercises and laboratory work. It has also increased the use of audio-visual material in education.
2. Computer in business

Fully used across the business sector — in department stores, restaurants, hotels and other retail centres — to process sales transactions, making them easy and accurate. Investors analyse investments, sales, income and expenses, markets and other aspects of business with them.
3. Computer in office

Used for writing letters, memos and notices, sending emails, scheduling meetings, and presenting business around the world through multimedia presentations. This has extended to mobile devices: professionals now read and answer email, open business files and update social media on the move.
4. Computer in communication

A computer is vital to communication and is the centrepiece of Information and Communication Technology (ICT). It is used for email, social media, video chat, websites, blogs, online conferencing and internet fax.
5. Computer in bank

Used for handling customer transactions, maintaining the ledger, issuing deposit receipts, making withdrawals and deposits, and providing online service to customers who want to know their balance. It is also used for online payments.

short.question: What is a computer?
short.answer:
A computer is a fast electronic data processing device. It takes in data, processes it according to the instructions given by the programmer or user, and produces the desired information as output at high speed.

The word comes from the Latin computare, meaning to calculate.

short.question: List out the characteristics of a computer.
short.answer:
There are five:

  1. Speed — it works far faster than a person, handling millions or billions of instructions a second.
  2. Accuracy — about 100%, provided the input is correct.
  3. Automation — once instructed, it carries on without human intervention.
  4. Diligence — repetitive work without boredom or tiredness.
  5. Versatility — different tasks in different fields, using different programs.

short.question: Define the term diligence of the computer.
short.answer:
Diligence means that a computer can perform repetitive tasks over and over without being bored and without ever getting tired. It will work as efficiently after several hours or days as it did at the start.

This is the feature that most obviously separates it from a person: the thousandth calculation is done with exactly the same care as the first.

short.question: List out the limitations of a computer.
short.answer:
1. It is a dull machine.
  2. It cannot think, and it cannot make the right decisions as a human being can.
  3. It cannot operate without electricity or a power supply.
  4. It cannot produce accurate output if the inputs are wrong.

long.question: Define accuracy and automation in relation to the computer.
long.answer:
Accuracy. A computer is more accurate than a person — its accuracy is about 100%. It does not miscopy a figure or lose count the way someone working by hand might.

But accuracy has a condition attached: the computer produces accurate output only if the inputs given to it are accurate. Incorrect input produces incorrect output, which is called GIGO — Garbage In, Garbage Out. So the accuracy belongs to the computer, while the responsibility for correct input belongs to the user.

Automation. A computer is an automatic machine. Once instructions are fed into it, it carries on working by itself without any human intervention, and it can perform a variety of jobs as long as there is a well-defined procedure for each. You set it going and it continues — nobody has to turn a handle.

The two are related: automation is what lets the computer work at speed, and accuracy is what makes the result worth having.

long.question: What do you mean by versatility?
long.answer:
Versatility is the ability to be used in different areas for different tasks, by running different programs. The same machine can do simple arithmetic and highly complex logical manipulation.

It is easiest to see in everyday use. At one moment a computer is playing music; at the same time it may be downloading from the internet while you work on a spreadsheet, a word processing document and a presentation. One device, many quite different jobs — that is versatility.

It is worth being precise about what it does not mean: versatility is about many different things, not many similar ones. A machine that does the same task a thousand times is showing diligence, not versatility.

long.question: Write down the capabilities and limitations of the computer.
long.answer:
Capabilities — what a computer can do:

  • It can perform a task automatically.
  • It can process with 100% accuracy.
  • It can perform different tasks in different fields.
  • It can perform repetitive tasks without getting tired.

Limitations — what it cannot do:

  • It is a dull machine.
  • It cannot think and make the right decisions as a human being can.
  • It cannot operate without electricity or a power supply.
  • It cannot produce accurate output if the inputs are wrong.

The lists mirror each other, and the contrast is the real lesson: a computer is superb at doing what it has been told, repeatedly and without error, and incapable of deciding what ought to be done. Everything on the capabilities list concerns carrying out instructions; everything on the limitations list concerns judgement and power.

long.question: Write down the application of computers in communication.
long.answer:
A computer is vital to communication, and is the centrepiece of Information and Communication Technology (ICT). Using the internet, it supports:

  • Email — sending messages and files to anyone, anywhere, in seconds.
  • Social media — keeping in touch with friends, family and colleagues.
  • Video chat — seeing and hearing the person you are talking to.
  • Websites and blogs — publishing to a wide audience.
  • Online conferencing — meetings with people in several places at once.
  • Internet fax — sending documents over the internet rather than a phone line.

What all of these have in common is that they turn distance into almost nothing: a computer lets you speak, write or meet someone on the other side of the world as easily as the person next door.

long.question: How can a computer be used in business and offices?
long.answer:
In business. Computers are used across the sector — in department stores, restaurants, hotels and other retail centres — to process sales transactions, making them easy and accurate. Beyond the till, investors use them to analyse investments, sales, income and expenses, markets and other aspects of the business, so that decisions rest on figures rather than guesswork.

In offices. Computers handle the everyday paperwork: writing letters, memos and notices, sending emails, and scheduling meetings. They are used to present the business to the world through multimedia presentations. And the office no longer has to be a room — professionals now read and answer email, open business files and update social media from mobile devices while away from their desks.

The thread through both is that the computer takes over the routine — recording, calculating, filing — and leaves people the deciding.

objective.question: Rewrite each incorrect statement to make it correct. (a) Computers are machines that were invented to play computer games and for entertainment purposes. (b) Information is the processed data. (c) Computer can produce accurate output if the inputs are inaccurate. (d) Computer gets tired and bored when it performs repetitive tasks. (e) Computers are used in the office for watching movies and playing games.
objective.answer:
(a) Incorrect. Computers are machines that were invented to help people solve problems and make tasks easier to do. (Games and entertainment are things a computer can do, but they are not why it was invented.)

(b) Correct as it stands. Information is refined, or processed, data.

(c) Incorrect. A computer can produce accurate output only when the inputs given to it are accurate. Wrong input gives wrong output — the GIGO rule.

(d) Incorrect. A computer never gets tired or bored: it can perform repetitive tasks for hours or days with the same accuracy. That is its diligence.

(e) Incorrect. Computers are used in the office for writing letters, memos and notices, sending emails, scheduling meetings and giving presentations.

objective.question: State whether the following statements are true or false. Rewrite each false statement to make it true. (a) The word "computer" comes from the Latin word "comput". (b) The accuracy of the computer is 100%. (c) Once instructions are fed to the computer, it works automatically without any human intervention. (d) A versatile machine means able to do many similar things. (e) The computer is a dull machine.
objective.answer:
(a) False. The word comes from the Latin computare, which means to calculate.

(b) True. A computer's accuracy is about 100% — provided the inputs are accurate.

(c) True. This is what automation means.

(d) False. A versatile machine is one able to do many different things in different areas, not many similar ones.

(e) True. The computer is a dull machine — it cannot think or make decisions the way a person can.

objective.question: Fill in the blanks with the appropriate word. (a) The computer processes … according to the … given by the user. (b) The computer is used to help people … and make tasks … to do. (c) The computer cannot work without … supply. (d) The computer is used in the bank for … (e) The computer is used in education for …
objective.answer:
(a) The computer processes input data according to the instructions given by the user.

(b) The computer is used to help people solve problems and make tasks easier to do.

(c) The computer cannot work without power supply (electricity).

(d) The computer is used in the bank for handling customer transactions — maintaining the ledger, issuing deposit receipts, and making withdrawals and deposits.

(e) The computer is used in education for learning — online classes, online examinations, online tutoring, e-books and lab work.

objective.question: Match the following. (a) Speed (b) Accuracy (c) Automation (d) Diligence (e) Versatility — with: millions of instructions per second; GIGO; functioning without user intervention; performing repetitive tasks without being tired; used in different areas for different tasks.
objective.answer:
CharacteristicMatches
(a) Speedmillions of instructions per second
(b) AccuracyGIGO
(c) Automationfunctioning without user intervention
(d) Diligenceperforming repetitive tasks without being tired
(e) Versatilityused in different areas for different tasks

Accuracy pairs with GIGO because both concern the link between input and output: a computer is accurate only when the input is, and GIGO is the name for what happens when it is not.

teaching_plan.activity: Ask the class what they used a computer for before school today. Collect the answers, then give the Latin origin and the definition. Draw the input → process → output cycle on the board and work through the terms in the definition.
Take each characteristic and ask for an example the pupils have seen. Spend time on accuracy and GIGO: enter a silly figure into a sum and show the silly answer that comes back.
Build two columns on the board. Ask what a computer can do, then what it cannot. Close on the point that everything on the "cannot" list involves judgement or power.

units.title: Computer Hardware
units.overview: This chapter discusses hardware components of a computer — input devices, processing unit, memory, output devices, and storage devices.
units.summary: Hardware refers to the physical parts of a computer. Key components include input devices (keyboard, mouse, scanner), the Central Processing Unit (CPU) that performs calculations, memory (RAM/ROM) for temporary/permanent storage, output devices (monitor, printer), and storage devices (hard disk, USB, CD). The CPU is the brain of the computer and contains the ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit) and Control Unit.

concepts.text: The physical parts of a computer that can be touched, such as keyboard, monitor, CPU, and memory.
Central Processing Unit — the brain of the computer. It has ALU (for arithmetic/logic) and CU (for control).
Input = data given to computer (keyboard). Output = result shown (monitor).
RAM = temporary (volatile). ROM = permanent (non-volatile).

very_short.a: Hardware is the physical components of a computer that can be touched.
CPU (Central Processing Unit) is the brain of the computer that performs processing.
Keyboard and mouse.

very_short.q: What is the full form of RAM?
very_short.a: Random Access Memory.

short.q: Explain the functions of the Central Processing Unit (CPU).
short.a: The CPU performs arithmetic and logical operations through the ALU, and directs the flow of data through the Control Unit. It executes instructions from memory and controls all other components.

short.q: Differentiate between RAM and ROM.
short.a: RAM is temporary, volatile, used while computer is on; ROM is permanent, non-volatile, stores BIOS and boot instructions.

long.q: Describe the major hardware components of a computer with their functions.
long.a: Major components: (1) Input devices (keyboard, mouse) — enter data. (2) CPU — processes data. (3) Memory (RAM/ROM) — stores data temporarily or permanently. (4) Output devices (monitor, printer) — show results. (5) Storage (HDD, SSD, USB) — long-term storage. (6) Motherboard — connects all parts.

detailed.heading: Chapter 2 — Computer Hardware
detailed.note: Notes for Chapter 2 of the Class 6 book: computer hardware.

blocks.text: Examples of input devices: keyboard, mouse, scanner, trackball, touchpad, joystick, bar code reader, digital camera, microphone, graphic digitizer, touch screen, QR code, and scanner. Central Processing Unit Arithmetic/Logic Unit

items: Keyboard The keyboard is the primary means of input by which the user can input the data. It looks like an electronic typewriter but contains more keys for specific purposes. Christopher Sholes invented the keyboard. Most keyboards have the following keys. Alphanumeric Keys (letters and numbers). Punctuation Keys (comma, semicolon, and so on). Special Keys (function keys, control keys, arrow keys, caps lock keys) and so on).

Mouse A computer mouse (pl. mice) is a hand-held pointing device that detects two-dimensional motion (X and Y axis) around the computer screen. Two rotating wheels (for X and Y axis) inside the mouse detect the movement and the direction of the mouse on the screen. By pressing the button of a mouse, the user communicates his/her choice to the computer. It is a small plastic box with two or three buttons on the top. It is used in the graphical user interface of a computer. Douglas Engelbart invented the computer mouse for the development of the basic graphical user interface (GUI). "Mouse" comes from the Sanskrit word "musuka".

Touchpad A touchpad or trackpad is a pointing device. It is one of the latest pointing devices. It looks like a small grey window, about two inches wide. The user slides his fingertip across the window to move the cursor on the screen. When the window is tapped, it works as the clicking of a mouse button. It is used in the latest laptops. Touchpad was invented by George E. Gerpheide.

Joystick A joystick is a pointing device that consists of a vertical handle like a gearshift lever mounted on a base with one or two buttons. It is used mainly for moving the object at high speed, thus it is used in playing video games, like, flight stimulation programs, car races, bike races, and in some computer-aided design systems. As the handle is moved around, the movement is translated into binary signals with the help of electronic contacts in its base. Joystick was invented by C. B. Mirick.

Touch Screen A touch screen is the assembly of both an input (touch panel) and output (display) device. A user can give input or control the information processing system through simple or multi-touch gestures by touching the screen with a special stylus or one or more fingers. The display is often an LCD (Liquid Crystal Display) or LED (Light Emitting Diode). Touch screens are commonly used in devices such as smartphones, personal computers, automated teller machines, electronic voting machines, handheld game consoles, and point-of-sale (POS) systems. Eric Arthur Johnson invented the touchscreen in 1965.

blocks.text: Central Processing Unit (CPU) is the brain of the computer. It is responsible for processing the inputs to produce the output and controlling all the operations of the computer. Components of CPU The CPU consists of mainly three components:

items: Arithmetic and Logic Unit (ALU): The ALU performs mathematical computations, and logic operations and controls the speed of those operations as directed by CU.

Control Unit (CU): The control unit of the CPU regulates the flow of data within the processor as the whole operations of the computer system. Hence, the CU acts as the nerve system of the computer system.

Register: The microprocessor has temporary data holding places called a register. Registers are small amounts of high-speed memory contained within the CPU. The main function of the register is to transfer data for immediate use by the CPU for data processing.

blocks.text: Memory unit or memory storage (in short; memory) is the main component of a computer system that enables it to function and it is used to store data/ instructions and programs temporarily in RAM and permanently in ROM and all storage devices. The digital computer contains two types of memory storage. Types of Memory The primary memory stores programs along with data temporarily (inside RAM), and stores necessary programs for the operation of the computer (ROM).
Primary memory is located between RAM and CPU. RAM, ROM, and Cache Memory are the primary memories.
Secondary Memory

Secondary storage is also called auxiliary memory or external or backup memory. It is a non-volatile memory that retains programs even if the Secondary memory (storage devices) stores operating systems, data, and application programs permanently. Hard disks, tape drives, CDs, DVDs, and solid-state drives are secondary storage devices.

The result after processing is called output. Output unit is responsible for providing the output after processing to the user. The outputs can be in the forms like text, image, audio, or video. There are two types of outputs:

items: Hardcopy output
Softcopy output

Softcopy refers to data that is shown on a display screen or sound produced by the speaker. This kind of output is untouchable. It is temporary. For example, contents displayed on a monitor or words spoken out by a voice response system(speaker) are soft copy outputs.

Hardcopy refers to output printed on paper that can be touched and carried for being shown to others. It is permanent and can be kept in paper files or can be looked at in the locker. For example, outputs produced on paper in the form of text or/and graphics by printers or plotters are hardcopy outputs.

blocks.text: Monitor

A computer monitor is an output unit, which displays information on the screen in pictorial or textual form. The display screen is used to view the result of the processing. It is the most common and popularly used output device for producing soft copy output. Different types of monitors are CRT Monitor, LCD Monitor, and LED Monitor.

items: CRT (Cathode Ray Tube) Monitor: It is a large bulky-sized monitor. It is rarely used at present. Due to its size, it is not appropriate for portable devices. Captain John Ericsson invented the computer monitor.

LCD (Liquid Crystal Display) Monitor: LCD is one of the common flat- panel monitors. It creates images with a special kind of liquid crystal. LCD is lighter in weight, not bulky but expensive compared to CRT monitors. It consumes low voltage and low power consumption than CRT. It is widely used in laptops, computers, digital cameras, digital clocks, digital watches, and CD players.

LED (Light Emitting Diode) Monitor: The LED monitor contains an array of light-emitting diodes as a video display. These diodes are turned on or off to display the output. Initially, it was used only for simple digital displays like the calculator and digital watch. At present, it is the popular monitor for television sets, desktop PC, laptops, mobile phones, and tablet PC.

blocks.text: Printer

The printer is a peripheral device used to print text, pictures, illustrations, permanent readable form. units.summary: Information and Communication Technology (ICT) includes tools that help people communicate, process, and share information. short.q: What are the advantages of ICT in education?

short.q: What is the importance of cyber law?
short.a: Cyber law protects users from fraud, hacking, identity theft, and misuse of data; it ensures safe and legal use of the internet.

long.q: Describe the applications of ICT and importance of cyber law.
long.a: ICT is used in communication (email, video), business (e-commerce), education (online learning), healthcare (telemedicine), and government (e-services). Cyber law ensures that digital activities are safe, legal, and protect personal and organizational data.

blocks.text: The World Wide Web also known as the web, WWW or W3. It is a giant collection of information that people can access through the internet. It is called the "World Wide Web" because it's available to people all over the world. Just like a spider's web connects different points, the World Wide Web connects different computers and devices all over the world. The Web was invented by Tim Berners-Lee at CERN in 1989 and opened to the public in 1991.

Browser (Web browser) is user-based application software that allows a user to interact with and display the webpages. It is the software that takes you anywhere on the Internet. Some of the popular browsers are Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Mozilla Firefox, Safari, Netscape Navigator, Opera, and Lynx.
Webpage

A webpage is a document that you can see on your computer or phone screen when you use the internet. A webpage is a part of a website; it means a website contains different hypertext webpages. It can be understood by an analogy "A Website is like a complete book, and a webpage is like a page of book". A webpage usually contains all sorts of things like text, pictures, videos, and information about different topics like animals, sports, or games.
You can click on links and buttons to explore the page and learn more about what you're interested in.
URL

A URL (Uniform Resource Locator) is a unique identifier used to locate a resource on the Internet. It is also referred to as a web address. A URL is a complete web address used to find a particular webpage. Example: https://www.asmitapublication.com/category/school-level/six
Website

A website is a collection of webpages that are all related to each other, just like a book with lots of pages. When you type a website's address into your internet browser, you'll see the first page of the website, called the homepage. From there, you can click on links to explore other pages on the website. For example, YouTube is a free global online video sharing and social media website that makes it easy to watch millions of different online videos.
You can even create and upload your own videos to share with others. Amazon is an another example of e-commerce website.

A search engine is a web-based software that helps the user to locate or access the required information from the Internet in an efficient manner. It uses powerful computers and algorithms to access the required content immediately. Some of the popular search engines used are google.com, yahoosearch. com, bing.com, ask.com, yandex.com, baidu.com, duckduckgo.com, and wow.com.

Email is like a letter that you send over the Internet. It sends information electronically from one computer to another computer through the Internet. It involves a sender and receivers. The email can be sent to two or more recipients. It can also add images, attach documents in the form of PDFs, audio, and video along with the message in text format. Every user has unique email address. The address will be used to send or receive the email.

blocks.text: The following are main features of spreadsheet software: It provides a way to organize and arrange data in rows and columns It makes calculations easy using formulae. Entry data and results can be obtained in pictorial form or various chart-pattern.
The following are basic fundamentals of spreadsheet software:

items: Cell In an Excel worksheet, a cell is an intersection between a column and a row, in which data can be stored. The cell is enclosed by a light-gray line known as a gridline. A cell can be identified by cell address, which is made up of a column heading and row number. The address of the first cell is A1.

Worksheet A worksheet or spreadsheet is an electronic sheet. It is the grid of vertical columns and horizontal rows that are combined to make a flat sheet and allows the storage/process of information. The Worksheet is a large working area where we can enter, edit and perform various kinds of data calculations. Worksheets can contain text, numbers, data, formulas, and charts too.
Workbook In Microsoft Excel, a workbook is a collection of one or more spreadsheets, also called worksheets, in a single file.

Cell Reference (Cell Address) A cell's location in the spreadsheet is referred to as its cell reference. To find a cell reference, simply look at the column headings to find which column the cell is in, and across to find which row it is in. The cell reference is a combination of the column letter and row number - such as A1, B2, or Z18. Especially, cell reference is very important while writing formulas or addressing the cell to evaluate the values.
Cell Range It is a collection of selected cells or a collection of several cells into a worksheet. Example: A1:A15.

Active Cell The active cell is the selected cell in which data is entered when you begin typing. Only one can be active at a time and is shown by a thick black border, which is called an active cell. The active cell is the cell surrounded by a black border. Data can only be entered into the active cell.

blocks.text: MS Excel is a commercial distributed by Microsoft Inc. This application file name is EXCEL.EXE and its extension is *.XLSX (Microsoft Office 2016) and the older extension. XLS was used up to MS-Excel 2003. Note: As application developed by Microsoft Inc. (MS Excel) is more popular, we are discussing features of application program by using MS Excel 2016. Choose Microsoft-Excel 2016. OR

Then a Run dialogue box will display.
Type the text Excel (not case sensitive) into Run box.

Then your required program Book1- Microsoft Excel will open. Then MS Excel 2016 screen appears on the screen. Click on the Blank Workbook to create a new Workbook. Now, a blank workbook opens and you can use as per your requirement.

The small black square in the lower- right corner of the selection. When you point to the fill handle, the pointer changes to a black cross.), you can quickly fill cells in a range with a series of numbers or dates or with a built-in series for days, weekdays, months, or years.

items: Select the first cell in the range that you want to fill.

Sorting is the process of arranging data in some logical data like alphabetical order, data in ascending or descending order. Sorting lists is a common spreadsheet task that allows you to easily reorder your data. To sort in alphabetical order

blocks.text: Mathematical Calculations in MS Excel Mathematical calculations are the major task performed in MS Excel. It can be used for various calculations like: addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, logical operations, etc. Formula can be used to perform calculations. Formula in MS Excel A formula is a sequence of values, cell references, and operators that produces a new value for existing values.
It is a mathematical instruction that can be used in MS Excel to perform calculations. Rules for using Formula in MS Excel

items: The formula must begin with an equals to sign (=).
After inserting formula, press Enter key to confirm it.
The formula is not case sensitive i.e., =C1+D1 is the same as =c1+d1.
The formula can include: numeric value, cell address, references, constants, operators and functions.

blocks.text: Functions in MS Excel MS Excel contains built-in/readymade formulas. The readymade formula is called a function. It allows performing any calculations quickly and easily. MS Excel supports different types of functions. The functions are categorized according to the work they do. Some commonly used functions are discussed below: Syntax: SUM(number1,number2,...) Multiplies all the numbers in a range of cells. Syntax:

PRODUCT(number1,number2,...) Returns the largest value in a set of values. Syntax: MAX(number1,number2,...) Returns the smallest number in a set of values. Syntax: MIN(number1,number2,...) Returns the average (arithmetic mean) of the arguments. Syntax: AVERAGE(number1, number2,...) Number1, number2,... are 1 to 255 numeric arguments for which you want the average. Examples of Mathematical Calculations Example 1: Calculate Total, Total Amount, VAT and Grand Total Procedure

items: To calculate Total, multiply the Rate and the Quantity. Click in the cell E2, type the formula =C2 * D2. Then press Enter key. Drag the formula in E2 downwards till cell E6 to calculate Total for all the particulars.

To calculate Total Amount in cell E7, add the Totals from cell E2 to E6. Click in the cell E7, type the formula = SUM (E2:E6). Total Amount can also be calculated using the formula = E2 + E3 + E4 + E5 + E6. Then press Enter key.

blocks.text: Charts in MS Excel Charts are the graphical presentation of numeric data in the worksheet. The data in the worksheet can be expressed in the form using a chart. As we change the data, the chart will be automatically updated. MS Excel contains different varieties of charts. They are: column, line, pie, bar, area and scatter chart. blocks.text: Change Chart Type You can easily change to a different type of chart at any time.

objective.question: State whether the following are true or false: MS Paint can only make single-layer bitmapped pictures. / The drawing canvas is the area in which the user will create and/or modify text only. / MS Paint has several pre-made shapes such as circles, squares, lines, and arrows that you can use to create your drawings. / You cannot edit images using MS Paint. / You cannot save your MS Paint images/drawings in a variety of file formats.
objective.answer:
(a) True. MS Paint can only make single-layer bitmapped pictures.
(b) False. The drawing canvas is the area in which the user creates and modifies drawings and pictures, not only text.
(c) True. MS Paint has several pre-made shapes such as circles, squares, lines, and arrows that you can use to create your drawings.
(d) False. You can edit images using MS Paint.
(e) False. You can save MS Paint images in a variety of file formats such as PNG, JPEG, BMP and GIF.

blocks.text: E-commerce (Electronic Commerce) is a way of buying and selling things using the Internet. It's like going to a store, but instead of walking in and browsing the shelves, buyers use a computer, tablet, or phone to look at pictures of the things they want to buy. Buyers can also read descriptions, see prices, add items to the virtual shopping cart, and enter the payment information to order. The orders will be delivered to their location.

Some of the common e-commerce service providers are daraz.com, sastodeal. com, meroshopping.com, and hamrobazar.com. M-commerce (Mobile commerce) is a type of commerce that happens on mobile devices like phones and tablets. It's like shopping online, but instead of using a computer, a mobile device is used. With M-commerce, things like clothes, toys, or games can be bought, and it can be done from anywhere, with the use of a phone and an internet connection.

Online payment is a way to buy things or send money using the internet. It's like sending a digital version of money that can be used to pay for things online. It can be used to buy things like clothes, games, movies ticket or music, or to send money to a friend or a family member. To make an online payment, one usually needs to have a special account, like a digital wallet or a prepaid card, which can be used to store money and make transactions.
Just like how physical money is used to buy things in a store, online payment can be used to buy things on websites or apps.

Cloud computing is a way of using the internet to store and access programs, files, and data. It's like having a big, virtual storage space that can be accessed from anywhere, as long as there is an internet connection. It can also be used to share files and collaborate with others, like working on a group project for school. Cloud computing is a great way to keep digital life organized and accessible, no matter where we are.

Artificial intelligence, or AI, is a type of computer technology that helps machines learn to think and make decisions as humans do. It's like having a robot friend that can learn new things and do tasks on their own. AI can do things like recognize the voice and respond to the user's commands, or help doctors diagnose illnesses more accurately. It can also help to play games, like chess or checkers, and even create art or music.

AI works by using complex algorithms and data to learn from experience and make predictions. Just like how we learn from our experiences and use our knowledge to make decisions, AI can learn from data and use that knowledge to help people solve problems and do tasks more efficiently.

Virtual reality, or VR, is a type of technology that lets the user feel like in a different world or place, even though the user is not there. It's like stepping into a video game or movie and being part of the action. With VR, the user wears a special headset that covers the eyes and ears and shows a virtual world that feels real. Users can move their heads and body to see the world around them change, just like in real life.

VR is great for games and simulations, like exploring space or diving into the ocean. It can also be used for education, like visiting historical landmarks or practicing surgery. VR is a fun way to explore new places and experiences, and it's becoming more and more advanced every day.

Mobile computing is a way of using technology on the go, using devices like phones, tablets, and laptops. It's like having a small computer with the user wherever he/she goes, that can be used to do things like play games, watch videos, or do homework. With mobile computing, the user doesn't have to be tied to a desk or a specific location to use technology. Users can use the phone to take pictures or record videos, or use a tablet to read books or draw pictures.
Mobile computing is great for kids because it's convenient and easy to use.
IoT

IoT stands for "Internet of Things" and it refers to a type of technology that connects different devices and objects to the Internet. It's like having everything in the house, from the toys to the kitchen appliances, connected to the internet and able to communicate with each other. With IoT, users can control different devices using a phone or a computer, and can also send information and alerts.
For example, users can use IoT to turn on the lights in the room with the voice or to receive a notification on the phone when the plants need watering. mila

blocks.text: Types of Programming Languages Different types of programming languages used are: Types of Programming Languages High-Level Language

items: Machine language: It is a first-generation language. The computer directly understands it. In this language, the program is developed by using the combinations of binary numbers (i.e., Os and 1s). So, it is not easy to create a program for humans. It is one of the low-level languages.

Assembly language:It is a second-generation language. This language uses mnemonics codes (abbreviation codes) to develop the program in place of binary numbers. Mnemonics is the short form of English terms, like ADD for addition, SUB for subtraction, and DIV for division. It is also a low-level language.

High-level language (HLL): It is the third, fourth, and fifth generation of programming languages. It uses simple English and mathematical statement for developing programs. So, it is easier to develop programs compared to machine and assembly language. Examples of high-level languages are QBASIC, FORTRAN, PASCAL, C, C++, Java, and Python.

blocks.text: QBASIC stands for Quick Beginner's All-purpose Symbolic Instruction Code. It is a programming language developed by Microsoft Corporation in 1985 AD. It uses keywords and mathematical symbols to write a program. A QBASIC program can contain more than one statement. A statement in QBASIC may be executable or non-executable. The executable statement performs actions e.g., PRINT, INPUT LET.

The non-executable statement does not show any action and does not form the sequence of execution e.g., REM, DIM, DECLARE, etc. It is a modular programming language i.e.; the program is divided into different modules. Features of QBASIC Programming Some major features of QBASIC are:

items: It is easier to understand.
It checks syntax automatically.
It keeps the same variable name in an identical form.
It capitalizes the reserved words too.

blocks.text: QBASIC Editor
The QBASIC editor allows you to write programs, view files, debug the program, automatically capitalize QBASIC keywords and run the program.

To open existing file To open the existing file click on file -> open and select the required file and click on OK. To exit from QBASIC To exit from QBASIC click on file -> Exit.

blocks.text: Some major elements of QBASIC programming are: Elements of QBASIC Programming Operators, Expression and Operands

items: Character Set QBASIC has a set of characters, which can be used in variables, constants, operators, and labels. A set of characters, which are valid in QBASIC is known as the QBASIC character set. The QBASIC character set consists of alphabets, numbers and special characters (*, &, >, etc.)
Keyword Keywords are reserved words, which have predefined meaning in QBASIC. Example: CLS, REM, INPUT, PRINT, LET, VAL.
Data Type Data is any value given to the program. Data are processed to get output in the program. Basically, QBASIC supports two types of data:
Numeric: only numbers
String: any alphanumeric values

blocks.text: Variable A variable is an entity that can be changed during the execution of the program. There are two types of variables in QBASIC: numeric and string variables. a. Numeric variable: In QBASIC numeric variables can be an integer, long integer, single-precision, or double-precision.

Type of Numeric 15, –26 A variable name followed with ! the sign indicates a single precision variable. b. String variable: A string variable is a variable, which stores string data i.e., alphanumeric data. A string variable can store 32767 characters. A string variable name must have a dollar ($) sign as the last character of the variable name. It may contain letters, digits, and periods. It must begin with a letter. It must not contain reserved words such as PRINT. Example:
Variable Declaration

In QBASIC variable can be declared by using two techniques: a. Implicit declaration: Implicit declaration is the default method of declaring variables in QBASIC. Using this method, we can declare a variable at the time of assigning value to the variable. One should take care of the type declaration symbol and use variables during the declaration.
